gaps.hint: verb needed with a singular subject (-ate)
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ate forms the verb: activate. The singular subject 'alarm' needs the -s form 'activates'.

gaps.sentence: The new bypass will be ___ (BENEFIT) to thousands of commuters.
gaps.explanation: 'Be beneficial to' — the adjective follows the verb 'be'.

gaps.sentence: Her ___ (PERFORM) in the final was outstanding.
gaps.explanation: After 'Her' a noun is needed: performance (-ance noun); performers are people.

gaps.sentence: He denied all knowledge of the ___ (APPEAR) of the documents.
gaps.explanation: The documents vanished, so the negative noun 'disappearance' is needed; 'appearance' means coming into view.

gaps.sentence: The crisis could ___ the economic situation (WORSE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -en forms the verb: worsen means to make worse. A base verb follows 'could'.

gaps.sentence: She gave a very ___ account of the incident that had everyone laughing (HUMOUR).
gaps.explanation: Everyone laughed, so the adjective is humorous (-ous). 'Humourless' means serious and would contradict the laughter.

gaps.hint: noun needed after 'His'; note the -al suffix
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'refuse' is 'refusal' (-al noun); 'refuse' as a noun means rubbish.

gaps.sentence: She was fired for ___ behaviour at work (PROFESSIONAL).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed before the noun 'behaviour'
gaps.explanation: The prefix un- forms the negative adjective: unprofessional behaviour is behaviour below professional standards.
